questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Owing for / his illness, / he couldn’t achieve / his goals.
questions.solution:
The erroneous segment is 'owing for'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__
;Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is not **grammatically correct. **
 
• The error lies in Part A of the sentence.
 
• Here, the error lies in the erroneous usage of the preposition 'for' after owing.
 
• The correct preposition after owing is 'to'.
 
• If something is owing to another thing, it is a result of that thing.
 
• Therefore, the correct substitution for the erroneous part is 'owing to'.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 3.**

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.

He had / prepare well / before the examination / so he did well.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**prepare well'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The verb 'prepare' should be in the past participle form ('prepared') after 'had' to correctly form the past perfect tense.
 
• The past perfect tense is used to indicate that an action was completed (finished or "perfected") at some point in the past before something else happened. In this case, the action of preparing had been completed befor
e the examination was faced,
 
• Thus, 'had prepared' instead of 'had prepare'.

 

Hence,** the correct answer** is, "He had prepared well before the examination, so he did well."
